rtlDecisions.question: In a horizontal slider in RTL, does ArrowRight increase or decrease the value?
rtlDecisions.apg: Right Arrow increases, Left Arrow decreases; no RTL statement. A note allows reversing the direction of value change where that is more intuitive.

libraries.behaviour: Reverses the horizontal axis in RTL: ArrowLeft increments, ArrowRight decrements; the thumb position is mirrored.
ArrowRight is -1 and ArrowLeft is +1 when rtl.
Back keys depend on slide direction: from-right (rtl, not inverted) treats ArrowRight as a back key.
ArrowRight steps by -1 and ArrowLeft by +1 when isRtl.
Slider turns reverse on by default for a horizontal slider in RTL; the handle then treats Left as +1 and Right as -1.

rtlDecisions.reason: The minimum sits at inline-start, so the track fills from the right in RTL and the arrow pointing toward the maximum must increase. All five libraries do this; a slider whose axis is physical (audio balance, a timeline that stays left-to-right) opts out per instance.

rtlDecisions.question: Do PageUp, PageDown, Home and End change meaning in an RTL horizontal slider?
rtlDecisions.apg: Home sets the first allowed value, End the last, Page Up increases by a larger step, Page Down decreases; no RTL statement.

libraries.behaviour: PageUp increments, PageDown decrements, Home sets the minimum, End the maximum, with no direction test.
PageUp +large step, PageDown -large step, Home minimum, End maximum, independent of rtl.
Home and PageDown are back keys in every slide direction.
PageUp +shiftStep, PageDown -shiftStep, Home min, End max, independent of isRtl.
Home is min, End is max, PageUp +2 steps, PageDown -2 steps, independent of direction.

rtlDecisions.reason: These keys name a value (smallest, largest, more, less), not a screen direction. All five libraries keep them fixed.

data.notes: RTL: in a horizontal slider the minimum is at inline-start, so ArrowLeft increases and ArrowRight decreases; ArrowUp/ArrowDown, PageUp/PageDown, Home and End keep their meaning in both directions and in both orientations. All five libraries studied behave this way. A test for the RTL variant: at value 50 with step 1, ArrowLeft gives 51, ArrowRight 49, ArrowUp 51, PageUp more than 51, Home the minimum. The page allows reversing the value direction when more intuitive; expose it as an explicit option for sliders whose axis is physical rather than textual (audio balance, a timeline that stays left-to-right), so a product can pin the LTR mapping. aria-valuetext must use the locale's digits and units.
